about: Index of the LOLA terrain for Godot (board M1-34). Heightmaps are r16 (see each region's .json); tiles are GLB LODs built by production/tools/build_terrain_tiles.py; sun_positions.json holds the dated light directions.
credit_line: Terrain made from NASA data: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation models from NASA Goddard's Planetary Geodynamics Data Archive (Barker et al. 2021, 2023) and the NASA PDS; Sun and Earth positions from NASA JPL Horizons. NASA does not endorse this game.
credit_line_short: Terrain made from NASA LRO LOLA data (GSFC PGDA / PDS); sky geometry from JPL Horizons.

aurora.name: Aurora Station (authored outpost) on the Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge

malapert_summit.name: Malapert relay summit (authored platform at the highest point of Mons Malapert)

cold_trap.name: Chapter 4 cold trap: a small permanently shadowed basin reached by a ridge road from Aurora

aurora_ridge.story: LOC-06 mast courtyard, Chapter 1 to 8 exteriors at Aurora

aurora_vista.story: horizon from Aurora: Shackleton, de Gerlache, the pole

cold_trap.story: LOC-09 surveyed approach and LOC-10 vault shelf (Chapter 4)

relay_road.story: LOC-11 relay road, 120 km in five playable segments (Chapter 8); 80 m vista grid, cut 10 m patches for the playable segments with make_terrain.window_m

relay_road_mid.story: LOC-11 relay route at the first repeater sector (EX-CH08-S03, S04): the playable 10 m patch around the computed relay road's midpoint, in that site's own frame so its Horizons rows light it (M1-87)

malapert_vista.story: horizon from the summit toward Earth

cold_trap_road.story: P-07 route B: 12 km ridge road, max 12 deg (game numbers from game-design/08_PUZZLE_DESIGNS.md; the computed road is evidence, not a replacement); routed on the full 20 m grid

relay_road.story: P-15 surveyed road: 120 km each way, max 12 deg (game numbers unchanged). The real summit plateau is ringed by slopes over 12 deg on the 80 m grid, so the last approach may use up to the VIPER design incline of 15 deg; the length above 12 deg is reported

frame: Godot X = map x - site x; Z = -(map y - site y); Y = height - site height. Azimuth 0 = local north (away from the pole), 90 = east (clockwise seen from above).
